entities.name: Ioannis Kolettis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ioannis Kolettis (d. 1847) was a pivotal figure in the nascent Greek state, serving as a physician, military leader during the Greek War of Independence (1821-1829), and a dominant politician in the early Greek Kingdom, notably as Prime Minister twice. His enduring legacy stems from his articulation of the "Megali Idea" (Great Idea), a potent irredentist vision for Greek territorial expansion that shaped national policy and identity for nearly a century, far beyond his death. He navigated the complex geopolitical landscape of the Eastern Question, balancing the interests of the Great Powers and the aspirations of the newly independent Greek nation.

Born in Suli, Epirus, around 1773-1774, Kolettis initially pursued a medical career, studying in Pisa and practicing in Ioannina under Ali Pasha. His involvement in the Philiki Etaireia led him to participate actively in the Greek Revolution from its earliest stages in Moldavia. After returning to Greece, he became a prominent leader of the Roumeliot (mainland Greek) faction, distinguishing himself in the civil conflicts of the 1820s and later serving in various ministerial roles under Ioannis Kapodistrias and King Otto. As Minister of the Interior, he oversaw critical administrative reforms and played a crucial role in establishing the capital in Athens. His diplomatic career included a significant tenure as ambassador to France from 1835 to 1843, where he cultivated support for Greek interests.
